records.label: Kallai pp.172–173: locate and date the pool

payload.claim: Does Kallai's particular pool satisfy a fixed east-of-tell and instruction-relevant phase branch at Kh. el-Marjama?

current_evidence.detail: Outcome recorded 19 October 2026: bearing-or-phase-miss, row not-east+undated. EVIDENCE: Kallai 1972 p. 172 puts the Byzantine church at the foot of the tell on its west side; p. 173 puts a water pool, with remains of its roofing vault, against the church on its east side. Kallai gives no size, construction or date for the pool, does not call it rock-cut and mentions no crypt. INFERENCE: the pool is at the western foot of the tell, not east of it. This excludes only the assignments that use Kallai’s pool (Koḥlit classes c06, c07, c09 and c10). It does not exclude the Marjama area, other pools or the Jericho classes. Whether this pool and Zohar’s church-crypt basin (IEJ 30 p. 219) are one feature is not settled.

freeze.detail: The arrival register froze the Kallai rows on 9 October 2026 (commit 6fee376), before the pages arrived, and the outcome record scores them as a test. This queue does not certify an unused observation: the church position was already exposed (Highlands p. 733), but the pool position east of the church was new.

payload.detail: EVIDENCE: Kallai p. 173 puts a water pool, with remains of its roofing vault, against the church on its east side. EVIDENCE: Kallai p. 172 puts the Byzantine church (14 × 10.5 m, mosaic floor) at the foot of the tell on its west side. This contradicts east-of-anchor only for the assignments that use this pool; it does not exclude other pools or features in the Marjama area. Until 19 October 2026 these pages were unread and this relation was unknown.

translation_context.text: In the {{ruin|e1-ruin}} that is in the {{Valley of Achor|e1-achor}}, under
the steps that go in toward the east,
{{forty cubits|e1-distance}}: a {{chest|e1-chest}} of silver and its vessels,
weighing seventeen talents. {{ΚΕΝ|e1-ken}}

variants.label: בחרובא: the ruin (Ḥorebbeh)
variants.note: Milik and Puech read a yod ('little ruin') and take it as the place Ḥorebbeh, later the monastery of Chorembe; Lefkovits, Lurie and Muchowski read a waw, and the text shown (חרובא) also has a waw. No published report describes a ruin with steps that fits, so the research files keep this entry at the level of the valley.

readings.meaning: 'little ruin'; Ḥorebbeh = monastery of Chorembe, near Kh. el-Mafjar
'little ruin'; name survives as the monastery of Chorembe
form with waw (gloss not given in the files)
form with waw (gloss not given in the files)

variants.label: שבעמק עכור: the Valley of Achor
variants.note: Reading עבור 'go past' would remove the valley altogether. Among those who read Achor, Milik and Puech follow the late tradition (Eusebius: 'north of Jericho', near Galgala) and place it in Wadi Nuweiʿimeh, while Allegro and Eshel prefer the Buqeia, the Iron Age valley; the research files rate Wadi Nuweiʿimeh best-supported but low for this entry and leave the choice open.

readings.meaning: Valley of Achor = Wadi Nuweiʿimeh, NE of Jericho (late tradition)
Wadi Nuweiʿimeh, NE of Jericho; rejects the Buqeia

variants.label: אמות {ארוה} ארבעין: the distance in cubits
variants.note: The word after 'cubits' is disputed: Puech reads a unit word, Lefkovits reads 'one', which makes the distance 41 cubits instead of 40, and Milik deletes it. The text shown marks the letters ארוה as cancelled, as Milik does; Lefkovits also reports Wolters's reading of I 2–3 in two different ways (p. 36 against p. 41 n. 58), and the files give no preference.

variants.label: שדת: a chest or a carrying chair
variants.note: The letters agree; the editors disagree on what kind of container held the silver. The files record both glosses and do not choose.

variants.label: ΚΕΝ: Greek letters
variants.note: All editions read the same letters, which follow 'seventeen talents'. As a Greek numeral ΚΕΝ would be 75, and the research files rule out the numeral idea; the personal-name idea stays open, and ΚΕΝ is the one group whose match with a name in Josephus carries some weight.

readings.meaning: Greek letters closing the entry; perhaps an abbreviated name
perhaps an abbreviated name; gap of 2–3 letters before it

translation_context.text: In the cistern that is under the {{wall|e10-wall}}, on the east,
in the {{spur of the rock|e10-rock}}: {{six|e10-six}} {{jars|e10-bars}} of silver.
{{Its entrance|e10-entrance}} is under the great threshold.

variants.label: החומא: the wall or rampart
variants.note: The word is read the same way; the open question is whether it is the wall of the city or of the Temple enclosure. The research files place the entry at the east wall beside the East Gate (best-supported, medium).

variants.label: בשן הסלע: the spur of the rock
variants.note: Milik's preliminary reading differed, but his DJD commentary speaks of a rocky projection, as the text shown does. The phrase 'spur of the rock' occurs in the Bible only at 1 Sam 14:4, and the lexicon rates its meaning high.

readings.meaning: a rocky projection under the east rampart

variants.label: כדין: bars or pitchers
variants.note: Puech reads bet ('bars'), Lefkovits kaf ('pitchers'); the same split recurs at VII 10 and IX 3. It changes the kind of silver deposit, not the place; the text shown has Lefkovits's כדין, and the files do not choose.

variants.label: שש: six
variants.note: Milik's preliminary publication gave 'six hundred' here. The files record it only as an early reading, and the text shown has שש, 'six'.

variants.label: ביאתו: its entrance
variants.note: In the Mishnah the word means 'entering', never an architectural entrance, so the lexicon rates 'entrance' as medium. Puech leaves open whether the entrance or the cache itself lies under the threshold.

readings.meaning: the entrance, or the cache itself, lies under the great threshold

translation_context.text: In the {{House of the Two Reservoirs|e55-bethesda}}, in the reservoir,
as you go in, {{on the right|e55-smallest-basin}}
of it: vessels of offering, eleven(?).
{{Their record beside them|g-ktbn}}.

variants.label: בבית אאשוחין: two reservoirs, or Bethesda
variants.note: Only Milik's emendation gives the name Bethesda, but the other reading still describes a double pool; the research keeps the Bethesda pools as best-supported (medium) while noting a second twin pool nearby. The text shown has אאשוחין, not Milik's אשדתין. In the plate check the fifth letter of the word looks like a ח rather than a ת, so the engraved letters favour 'reservoirs' and Milik's Bethesda needs at least one correction (Q26).

readings.meaning: rejects Bethesda; the site 'not completely certain'

variants.label: לימינ{מ}ית: the smallest basin?
variants.note: Milik's and Puech's word for the smallest basin fits a twin pool with a smaller basin; Lefkovits reads a basin and a measure instead. The text shown has לימינ{מ}ית, which matches none of these readings; the translation follows it ('on the right'), and the atlas landmark follows Milik and Puech (2015 pp. 94, 103).

readings.meaning: its smallest basin, which one can enter
the smallest basin (at Bethesda, the northern one)

translation_context.text: In the {{entrance|e56-entrance-or-alley}} of the {{[ledge]|e56-course}} of the {{western resting chamber|e56-burial-chamber}},
a {{platform(?)|e56-platform}} on {{◦ […]|e56-cave}}: nine hundred;
of gold, 5 talents; {{sixty talents|e56-division}}. {{Its entrance is from the west|e56-from-west}}.
Under the black stone: {{juglets|e56-juglets}}. Under the threshold of
the {{cistern|e56-niche-or-cistern}}: 42 talents.

variants.label: במבא: entrance, or alley
variants.note: In the Bible the word mostly means 'entrance'; every Mishnah example is מבוי 'alley', the sense Lefkovits takes. The research lexicon rates the meaning medium.

variants.label: רובד: course or terrace (restored)
variants.note: The research lexicon marks this word as restored at XI 16 and rates its meaning medium. The text shown restores it too, in brackets.

readings.meaning: pavement, terrace; restored on this line

variants.label: בית המשכב: the burial chamber?
variants.note: The phrase בית משכב does not occur in the Bible, and only a few uses of משכב are funerary. The research lexicon rates the meaning low to medium.

variants.label: טיף: platform?
variants.note: The word is not attested in this sense in the Bible or the Mishnah. The research lexicon rates 'platform' low.

variants.label: מ: the cave (restored)
variants.note: Only the מ survives; Puech restores 'cave', and his printed text and commentary spell the restoration differently. The files report no other editor's reading of this spot. The text shown leaves the spot unread; the atlas description's cave follows Puech.

variants.label: ככרין ששין: Milik's new item
variants.note: Milik, followed by Pixner, Wolters, García Martínez, Vermes and Wise, splits entry 56 into three deposits and moves ככרין ששין and בידן into the following item; Puech and Lefkovits keep one entry. Separate deposits could lie at separate spots (Q6).

readings.meaning: three items; this sum opens his item 59

variants.label: ביאתו מן המערב: entrance from the west
variants.note: The direction changes with the reading. The text shown has מן המערב, as Puech; the research lexicon rates ביאה 'entrance' medium.

variants.label: כוזין: juglets
variants.note: Wolters says the original in Amman and two published facsimiles support כוזין. The text shown has כוזין, not Milik's בידן.

variants.label: הבור: cistern, or burial niche
variants.note: The landmark changes from a tomb feature to a water installation. The text shown has Milik's הבור; the research lexicon rates כוך medium. The translation follows the text shown ('the cistern'); the atlas description's recesses follow Puech.

readings.meaning: a burial niche; the document's tomb words are קבר, משכן and בית המשכב

translation_context.text: In the {{great drain|e59-great-conduit}} of the {{cistern|e59-bezek}}, {{inside the cistern|e59-house}}:
the whole weight, 71 talents and twenty minas.

variants.label: בביבא הגדולא: the great conduit
variants.note: The word is agreed apart from a reading bkwkʾ that Puech rejects, and the research lexicon rates ביב 'conduit, drain' medium-high. Zertal's survey reports cisterns and burial caves but no conduit at either Kh. Ibziq site (2008, Vol. 2 pp. 191–198).

variants.label: הבור: Bezek, or another name
variants.note: Only the Bezek reading gives a place the research can test: Kh. Ibziq, rated possible, medium, or Kh. Salhab, rated possible, low, where Zertal places biblical Bezek (2008, Vol. 2 pp. 104–107, 151–153). Zertal finds the name at Ibziq only from the Byzantine period. Milik's reading points to Hebron. The text shown has הבור, the letters of Wilmot and Wise, not Puech's הבזך; the translation follows the letters shown ('cistern'), and the atlas placement follows Puech.

readings.meaning: ha-Bezek = Kh. Ibziq, 'for lack of anything better'
ha-Baruk: Banî Naʿîm and Hebron; in the Addenda, Hebron

variants.label: מלבית הבור: house of Bezek, or tomb
variants.note: The second instance may read bzk or kwk, so this is either a building named for Bezek or a burial chamber near the conduit. A kokhim tomb of the 1st–2nd centuries CE was excavated at Kh. Ibziq in 1971 (HA 40 p. 22); it matches in type and period but does not identify the chamber. Lower Ibziq also has about 70 undated burial caves (Zertal 2008, Vol. 2 pp. 191–193). The text shown again has הבור.

readings.meaning: 'the house of Bezek' or 'the burial chamber'

variants.label: המלח: the Millo, the Esplanade or salt
variants.note: Puech 2015 and Lefkovits adopt a salt-related pit below steps. Puech also discusses mixing/dissolving and retains the ha-Melah/Millo alternative; Lefkovits lists furnace, burial-niche and named-pit alternatives in his apparatus. The atlas Millo/Tyropoeon placement depends on the selected lexical/site branch. Salt association does not require a saline spring. Steps entering a pit do not alone establish the specified below-steps relation. The numeral gives treasure quantity, not distance or depth.

readings.meaning: salt-related pit below steps; mixing/dissolving and ha-Melah alternatives discussed
salt pit adopted; other feature types discussed in apparatus

variants.label: 41: the sum in talents
variants.note: The research files give this sum as 42 talents and list no edition that reads it differently. The numeral signs in the text shown add up to 41 (20 + 20 + 1), so the figure here differs from all three editions as the files report them.

readings.meaning: same as Puech (not among the six numeral differences)
same as Puech (not among his numeral differences)

variants.label: ΗΝ: Greek letters
variants.note: All editions read ΗΝ. On standard values it is 58, and the research files rule out Ullendorff's numeral readings because they need at least four different rules for five groups.

readings.meaning: gap of about 4 letters before it

translation_context.text: In the pit that is {{on the north side|e60-janoah}} of {{Koḥlit|e60-kohlit}}, {{its opening to the north|e60-opening}},
with tombs at its mouth: {{a copy of this document|e60-duplicate}},
and its explanation, and their measurements, and the details of
each and every one.

variants.label: שב{צח}צפון: situated, Smooth Rock, or Janoah
variants.note: Only the Janoah reading would add a second place name beside Koḥlit; Puech rejects it and the research leaves it open (Q12). The text shown shows Milik's צח as cancelled letters, leaving שבצפון. The plate check found a box letter and a nun-like letter after ש, then a letter at a fold and a clear בצפון, with no צ and no yod between the box letter and the nun; that fits Puech's 'situated' better than Janoah or Milik's Smooth Rock, without deciding between bet and kaf (Q12).

readings.meaning: situated; rejects Janoah on the engraving
the tunnel in the Smooth Rock

variants.label: כחלת: Koḥlit
variants.note: Koḥlit remains geographically unidentified. Rabbinic name witnesses recorded in the research are unlocated; no decisive outside location witness is established. Tell es-Sultan stays possible/low. Carmel, Transjordan and Samarian proposals cannot be rejected solely by entry order. See the source-specific cycle7 screen.

readings.meaning: Tell es-Sultan (old Jericho), as a hypothesis
Tell es-Sultan, north of Hasmonaean and Herodian Jericho
Tell es-Sultan, if Achor is Wadi Nuweiʿimeh

variants.note: Puech reads the pit's opening as hidden, Milik as facing north. Lefkovits prints צפון in line XII 11, which the findings log lists as an error.

variants.note: The research files say only that the last entry holds the duplicate document, so the list ends where it keeps its key. They report no editor's disagreement over these closing words.

translation_context.text: In the cave of the old {{House of Washing(?)|e7-house}}, on the third
{{ledge|e7-course}}: sixty-five ingots of gold. {{ΘΕ|e7-the}}

variants.label: בית המדח: the house of MDH
variants.note: The files report the key word four ways (המדה, המרה, המדח, חמדה); the text shown has המדח. The name is not anchored in any ancient text, the lexicon rates it low, and the files keep only the Temple area as a possible setting. The translation follows the letters shown ('Washing(?)', as Høgenhaven); the atlas title 'House of Tribute' follows Puech. Lefkovits 2000 prints חמדה ('Old Beth Ḥemdah', p. 106) but states that every letter of the word is ambiguous (p. 110). Plate check round 2 (16 Oct 2026): the fourth letter leans to ה, against Wolters's ח; the first (ה/ח) and third (ד/ר) are undecided (tables/plate_check.csv).

readings.meaning: 'house of Tribute'; the sense 'measure' is 'out of place'
'Old Beth Ḥemdah'; each of the four letters can be read two or three ways (he/ḥet/taw, mem/bet, dalet/reš, he/ḥet/taw), 36 combinations

variants.label: ברובד: on the course or terrace
variants.note: The lexicon rates the meaning as medium; its parallels are in the Mishnah (m. Middot 3:6; 4:4; m. Yoma 4:3). The files record no editor who reads the letters differently.

variants.label: ΘΕ: Greek letters
variants.note: ΞΕ would equal 65, the number of gold ingots in the line, but both facsimiles show a Θ, and the research files do not let a numerical coincidence choose the reading. The Theboutis link rests on two letters that begin 43 names in Josephus, so it is weak. The plate check found a closed ring with a central bar, a Θ, not the three bars of a Ξ.

readings.meaning: the numeral 65, the amount in the line

{{nineteen cubits|e9-distance}} away: in it are vessels,
and in its {{channel(?)|e9-channel}}: ten talents. {{ΔΙ|e9-di}}

variants.label: השער המזרחי: the East Gate
variants.note: All editions read the same words; the question is which gate. The research files follow the Temple's East Gate (best-supported, medium) and did not adopt Thiering's Qumran door.

readings.meaning: the Golden Gate, only eastern exit of the Temple enclosure
can only be the Temple's East Gate
city East Gate (Neh 3:29) or Temple Eastern Gate (m. Middot)
in the Temple area; Jerusalem is never named

variants.label: אמות תשע עסרא: the distance from the gate
variants.note: The distance from the gate differs between the two editions. The text shown reads תשע עסרא, nineteen, as Lefkovits does, not Puech's fifteen; the files give no preference.

variants.label: ובמזקא: and in the channel
variants.note: The lexicon rates 'channel' as medium, and Allegro and Luria read other letters. Milik and several others make the channel a separate hiding place from the cistern, while Puech and Lefkovits keep one entry; the files leave that open.

readings.who: Pixner; Wolters; García Martínez; Vermes; Wise

variants.label: ΔΙ: Greek letters
variants.note: All editions read ΔΙ, which stands where the editors disagree about whether a new hiding place begins. As a numeral it would be 14, not the ten talents of the line, and the research files reject Ullendorff's mix of rules.

payload.label: בשית האדמא: the earth pit
payload.note: האדמא can mean 'earth' or 'red'. Red marl is common in the area (Puech 2015 p. 52 n. 206), so both senses fit the terrain in kind; no pit is reported.

readings.meaning: 'earth pit': dug in ground, not rock

payload.label: הצופא מזרח: what faces east?
payload.note: Milik attaches the eastward aspect to the cave. The scene places both mouths facing east as a stricter model choice. The displayed unvocalized wording does not independently settle the attachment. “Northern opening” identifies the northern member of the pair, without requiring a north-facing mouth. Puech 2015 is directly verified to pp. 59–60; the original Lefkovits apparatus remains pending. Puech supplies the direction article as an editorial correction, gives no explicit directional-attachment argument and separately discusses pillar versus terrace; these model alternatives are not a newly verified editorial disagreement. Twin Cave’s report separately describes both mouths facing east; IV/17’s eastern-cliff location does not by itself give mouth bearings.

readings.meaning: the cave has two entrances and faces east
readings.ref: p. 140, item 27; p. 147, Col. VI, l. 1

readings.meaning: eastward aspect follows the two-opening cave description; no explicit requirement that both mouths face east in the commentary

payload.label: שב{צח}צפון: situated, Smooth Rock, or Janoah
payload.note: Only the Janoah reading would add a second place name beside Koḥlit; Puech rejects it and the research leaves it open (Q12). The text shown shows Milik's צח as cancelled letters, leaving שבצפון. The plate check found a box letter and a nun-like letter after ש, then a letter at a fold and a clear בצפון, with no צ and no yod between the box letter and the nun; that fits Puech's 'situated' better than Janoah or Milik's Smooth Rock, without deciding between bet and kaf (Q12).

the tunnel in the Smooth Rock

limits: This is a new derived exploratory dataset, built from previously exposed registries and protocol. No new primary image, archaeological observation, custodian reply or holdout is asserted.
Pair counts describe finite logical alternatives after nuisance/equivalence collapse. They supply neither probabilities, confidence, regional rarity nor cross-project utility.

Guaranteed pair separation means disjoint compatible decisive-outcome sets conditional on every observation gate succeeding. A possible unresolved result prevents unconditional guaranteed identification.
Nuisance windows are unioned within assignment/reading families before identical signatures collapse. Model weights and duplicated parameter branches cannot increase influence.

Joint sets preserve the explicit nuisance-branch correlations; unrecorded within-branch correlations remain unknown. Different classes can have overlapping predictions, and an unknown expands to every decisive outcome. Partial empirical results require an explicit outcome-set preview rather than a forced category.

The seven acquisition tasks in the existing queue concern several independent claims. Their generic compatible/contradicted gate outcomes cannot be treated as mutually exclusive predictions of Koḥlit sites.

The finite Koḥlit roster is an implementation pilot, not a regional denominator. All equally available geographic alternatives, an independently reserved prediction and exposure audits remain necessary for identification.

Named dependency means a conditional plan with a precise source route; record survival, usability, access and timing are unverified. Unscoped dependencies are excluded from the named-dependency scenario.
No plans, requests, historical outcomes, rarity registrations, atlas data or deposit statuses are changed by this planner or an outcome preview.

The three letter observations share an image acquisition bundle and reader gates; observational component count is different from acquisition count. Existing frozen full-word success conditions still require every component to be decisive.
